questions.question: Explain the hydrolytic ring-opening polymerisation mechanism of Nylon-6.
questions.solution_html:
• Nylon-6 is prepared by the hydrolytic ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam. In the first step
  • caprolactam reacts with water to form aminocaproic acid. This step involves the opening of the cyclic
  • amide ring structure. The formed amino acid then undergoes condensation polymerization. Repeated
  • condensation reactions lead to the formation of long polymer chains. The process results in the formation
  • of amide linkages between monomer units. Water is eliminated during the condensation step.
  • 25901152

questions.question: Compare solution polymerisation and emulsion polymerisation.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare solution polymerisation and emulsion polymerisation.
  • Solution polymerization is carried out in a suitable solvent where both monomer and initiator are soluble.
  • Emulsion polymerization is carried out in water using surfactants to form micelles. In solution
  • polymerization, the polymer remains dissolved in the solvent. In emulsion polymerization, the polymer is
  • obtained as a latex. The rate of polymerization is generally slower in solution polymerization. Emulsion
  • polymerization has a faster reaction rate due to high surface area. Heat control is difficult in solution
  • polymerization. emulsion polymerization provides better heat control.
questions.final_answer: polymerization. emulsion polymerization provides better heat control

questions.question: Explain in detail the classification of polymers based on origin and structure.
questions.solution_html:
• Polymers can be classified based on their origin and structure. Based on origin, polymers are divided into
  • natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic polymers. Natural polymers occur in nature and include materials
  • like cellulose and proteins. Semi-synthetic polymers are chemically modified natural polymers such as
  • cellulose acetate. Synthetic polymers are man-made and include plastics like polyethylene and PVC.
  • Based on structure, polymers are classified as linear, branched, and cross-linked polymers. Linear
  • polymers are the polymers where monomeric units are linked together to form long straight chains. The
  • polymeric chains are stacked over one another to give a well packed structure. As a result of close
  • packing, such polymers have high densities, high tensile strength and high melting points. Common
  • examples of these type polymers are polyethylene, polyester and nylon etc.
  • Branched Chain Polymers: In this type of polymers, the monomeric units are linked to constitute long
  • chains, which are also called main-chain. There are side chains of different lengths which constitute
  • branches. Branched chain polymers are irregularly packed and thus, they have low density, lower tensile
  • strength and lower melting points as compared to linear polymers. Amylopectin and glycogen are
  • common examples of such type.
  • 25901152
  • EXAMINATION March 2026
  • Fourth SEMESTER Discipline Specific Elective (DSE) - MG4DSECHE200 - POLYMER
  • CHEMISTRY
  • Cross-Linked Polymers or Network Polymers: In this type of polymers, the monomeric units are linked
  • together to constitute a three dimensional network. The links involved are called cross links. Cross-linked
  • polymers are hard, rigid and brittle because of their network structure. Common examples of this type of
  • polymers are bakelite, formaldehyde resin, melamine, etc
questions.final_answer: polymers are bakelite, formaldehyde resin, melamine, etc
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain in detail the practical significance of polymer molecular weight?
questions.solution_html:
• Molecular weight is an important parameter that determines the properties of polymers. It affects the
  • mechanical strength of the material significantly. Polymers with high molecular weight generally have
  • higher strength and toughness. It also influences the viscosity of polymer solutions and melts. Higher
  • molecular weight leads to increased viscosity. The melting point and glass transition temperature are also
  • affected by molecular weight. As molecular weight increases, thermal stability improves. Molecular
  • weight also affects the processability of polymers. High molecular weight polymers are difficult to
  • process due to their high viscosity. Low molecular weight polymers are easier to process but have lower
  • strength. Molecular weight is measured using number average and weight average methods. It is
  • important in industrial applications for quality control. It helps in selecting suitable polymers for specific
  • uses.
questions.final_answer: uses
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the properties and applications of PMMA.
questions.solution_html:
• Polymethyl methacrylate is a transparent thermoplastic polymer. It is commonly known as acrylic or
  • organic glass. PMMA has excellent optical clarity and allows transmission of light. It is lightweight
  • compared to glass and has good impact resistance. The polymer shows good weather and UV resistance.
  • However, it is brittle and can crack under stress. PMMA has good electrical insulating properties. It is
  • easy to mold and shape into different forms. It is widely used as a substitute for glass. Applications
  • include lenses, windows, and display panels. It is used in aircraft windows due to its light weight. It is
  • also used in signboards and decorative items. PMMA is used in medical devices and optical instruments.
questions.final_answer: also used in signboards and decorative items. PMMA is used in medical devices and optical instruments

  • polymerization, the polymer remains dissolved in the solvent. In emulsion polymerization, the polymer is
  • obtained as a latex. The rate of polymerization is generally slower in solution polymerization. Emulsion
  • polymerization has a faster reaction rate due to high surface area. Heat control is difficult in solution
  • polymerization. emulsion polymerization provides better heat control.
questions.final_answer: polymerization. emulsion polymerization provides better heat control

questions.question: Explain in detail the classification of polymers based on origin and structure.
questions.solution_html:
• Polymers can be classified based on their origin and structure. Based on origin, polymers are divided into
  • natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic polymers. Natural polymers occur in nature and include materials
  • like cellulose and proteins. Semi-synthetic polymers are chemically modified natural polymers such as
  • cellulose acetate. Synthetic polymers are man-made and include plastics like polyethylene and PVC.
  • Based on structure, polymers are classified as linear, branched, and cross-linked polymers. Linear
  • polymers are the polymers where monomeric units are linked together to form long straight chains. The
  • polymeric chains are stacked over one another to give a well packed structure. As a result of close
  • packing, such polymers have high densities, high tensile strength and high melting points. Common
  • examples of these type polymers are polyethylene, polyester and nylon etc.
  • Branched Chain Polymers: In this type of polymers, the monomeric units are linked to constitute long
  • chains, which are also called main-chain. There are side chains of different lengths which constitute
  • branches. Branched chain polymers are irregularly packed and thus, they have low density, lower tensile
  • strength and lower melting points as compared to linear polymers. Amylopectin and glycogen are
  • common examples of such type.
  • 25901152
  • EXAMINATION March 2026
  • Fourth SEMESTER Discipline Specific Elective (DSE) - MG4DSECHE200 - POLYMER
  • CHEMISTRY
  • Cross-Linked Polymers or Network Polymers: In this type of polymers, the monomeric units are linked
  • together to constitute a three dimensional network. The links involved are called cross links. Cross-linked
  • polymers are hard, rigid and brittle because of their network structure. Common examples of this type of
  • polymers are bakelite, formaldehyde resin, melamine, etc
questions.final_answer: polymers are bakelite, formaldehyde resin, melamine, etc

questions.question: Explain in detail the practical significance of polymer molecular weight?
questions.solution_html:
• Molecular weight is an important parameter that determines the properties of polymers. It affects the
  • mechanical strength of the material significantly. Polymers with high molecular weight generally have
  • higher strength and toughness. It also influences the viscosity of polymer solutions and melts. Higher
  • molecular weight leads to increased viscosity. The melting point and glass transition temperature are also
  • affected by molecular weight. As molecular weight increases, thermal stability improves. Molecular
  • weight also affects the processability of polymers. High molecular weight polymers are difficult to
  • process due to their high viscosity. Low molecular weight polymers are easier to process but have lower
  • strength. Molecular weight is measured using number average and weight average methods. It is
  • important in industrial applications for quality control. It helps in selecting suitable polymers for specific
  • uses.
questions.final_answer: uses
